page: Amazon Web Services i4g.2xlarge is an arm64 storage-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor. The system is driven by an AWS Graviton2 processor using the ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 microarchitecture, supplying 8 physical cores and 8 dedicated vCPUs operating at 2.5 GHz with a single thread per core. Memory allocation totals 64.0 GB of RAM, providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio backed by 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache per core, and 64 KB of L1 data cache. The instance includes 1875 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD storage and provides a baseline network throughput of 5 Gbps, with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses included.

Benchmark evaluations indicate consistent mid-tier performance across multi-threaded and I/O-adjacent tasks. Multi-core performance is highlighted by a stress-ng multi-core metric of 12132.09 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 5360.0, both placing in the average tier. Memory bandwidth achieves 116.33 GB/sec on uncached large-block reads and 472.81 GB/sec on cached reads. In real-world operational benchmarks, the instance yields 9.8 million operations per second in Redis SET tests, 5224.61 in PassMark database operations, and 9.71 GB/sec in static web throughput. Single-core compute and intensive compression, such as single-threaded bzip3 decompression at 7.19 GB/sec, fall into the bottom tier.

By coupling an energy-efficient ARM processor architecture with 1875 GB of integrated high-speed NVMe flash and an ample 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, the i4g.2xlarge delivers resource-dense efficiency without the overhead of standalone remote storage attachments. This configuration is structurally suited for I/O-intensive transactional databases, NoSQL distributed data stores, in-memory caching engines, search indices, and high-throughput logging systems that benefit from fast local storage and memory density over high single-threaded IPC.
description: Amazon Web Services i4g.2xlarge is a storage-optimized instance based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 architecture. It features 8 dedicated physical vCPUs running at 2.5 GHz alongside 64.0 GB of RAM, offering an 8.0 GB per vCPU memory density. Bundled with 1875 GB of high-speed local NVMe SSD storage and a 5 Gbps baseline network interface, it does not incorporate a discrete GPU. In benchmark assessments, it demonstrates solid multi-core execution and I/O throughput, posting 9.8 million Redis SET operations per second and stable database operations, despite lower single-threaded compression performance. The architectural synergy between dense local NVMe storage, dedicated Graviton cores, and substantial memory capacity makes it well-matched for NoSQL databases, transactional data stores, search indexing, and real-time caching systems.
